designSummary: Cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study; each adult is classified by code and by laboratory results at 30 June 2026.
sampleSize: About 38,000 adults are registered; if 60 percent have at least two eGFR results and 9 percent of those meet laboratory criteria, about 2,050 adults have laboratory-defined disease. With a sensitivity near 60 percent, 2,050 cases give a 95 percent confidence interval about 2.1 percentage points either side; the subgroup aged 80 or over (about 600 cases) gives about 4 points either side, enough to separate 50 from 70 percent. The study uses every eligible adult; no sampling is needed except for the 200-record review.
primaryAnalysis: Sensitivity with a Wilson 95 percent confidence interval, pooled across practices, with per-practice estimates shown.
secondaryAnalysis: Positive predictive value, specificity and negative predictive value; sensitivity by age band, sex and stage; reasons for discordance from the 200-record review.
missingData: Adults with a single eGFR result are excluded from the primary estimate and reported with their coding status; a sensitivity analysis counts coded adults with a single low result as false positives.
multiplicity: One primary estimate; subgroups reported with intervals and no significance tests.
software: R; the classification rule and code are fixed before the extract is opened.
overfittingGuards: Reference standard rule fixed before extraction
Subgroups limited to age band, sex and stage
No threshold search on eGFR values
summary: All eligible adults; about 2,050 cases give a precise sensitivity estimate and useful precision in the oldest group.
